items.en: The Nine Contemplations: What They Counteract, Their Classification, and the Path
items.zh: 九想 · 對治 · 攝法 · 趣道

zh: 二、明九想對治者，行者修九想既通，必須增想重修，令觀行熟利。隨所觀時，心即與定相應，想法持心，無分散意，此則能破六欲，除世貪愛。六欲者：一者、色欲；二、形貌欲；三、威儀姿態欲；四、言語音聲欲；五、細滑欲；六、人相欲。此六欲中能生六種著。色欲者，有人染著赤色，若赤白色，若黃白色、黑色，若赤黑色，若青色，若青白色，若桃華色。無智愚人見此等色，沒溺迷醉。若形貌欲，有人但著形貌，面如滿月，修目高眉，細腰纖指，相好端嚴，心即惑著。威儀欲者，有人著威儀姿態，行步汪洋，揚眉頓臉，含笑嬌盈，便生愛染。
en: Second, clarifying what the nine contemplations counteract: the practitioner, having already penetrated the nine contemplations, must further add to and repeatedly cultivate this perception, so that the practice of contemplation grows mature and sharp. Whenever one contemplates in this way, the mind thereupon corresponds with concentration, the dharma of perception holding the mind fast, without any scattering of intent — this, then, is able to break through the six desires and remove worldly craving and attachment.

The six desires are: first, desire for color; second, desire for form and appearance; third, desire for demeanor and bearing; fourth, desire for speech and voice; fifth, desire for smooth touch; sixth, desire for the human mark itself. Within these six desires, six kinds of attachment are able to arise.

As for desire for color: some people are stained with attachment to red, or to reddish-white, or to yellowish-white, or to black, or to reddish-black, or to blue-green, or to bluish-white, or to a peach-blossom hue. The unwise and foolish, seeing colors of this kind, sink and drown, bewildered and intoxicated. As for desire for form and appearance: some people are attached only to form and appearance — a face like the full moon, long eyes, high brows, a slender waist, delicate fingers, features fine and upright — the mind is thereupon bewildered and attached. As for desire for demeanor: some people are attached to demeanor and bearing — a gait broad and graceful, brows raised, cheeks dimpling, a smile held with coy allure — this thereupon gives rise to love and attachment.

zh: 言語欲者，有人但愛語聲，若聞巧言華說，應意承旨，音詞清雅，歌詠讚歎，悅動人心，愚夫淺識，為之迷惑。細滑欲者，有人但愛身形柔軟，肥膚光悅，猶若兜羅之綿，寒時體溫，熱時體涼，按摩接待，身服熏香，凡情沒溺，為此危喪。雜欲者，有人皆著五事。人相欲者，有人皆不著五事，但著人相。若男若女，雖見上五事，若不得所愛之人，猶不染著；若遇適意之人，則能捨世所重，頓亡軀命。如是六欲，世世誑惑眾生，沈淪生死，沒溺三塗，不得解脫。若能善修九想對治除滅，則六欲賊破散，疾證涅槃。
en: As for desire for speech: some people love only the sound of speech — hearing clever words and flowery phrases, words that answer to the listener's mind and defer to the listener's wishes, the tone and diction clear and elegant, songs of praise and admiration, stirring and delighting the heart — the foolish and shallow of understanding are thereby bewildered by it. As for desire for smooth touch: some people love only a body soft and smooth to the touch, its flesh full and radiantly glossy, like tūla cotton — warm to the touch in the cold, cool to the touch in the heat, welcoming to massage and embrace, the body scented with fragrant perfume — the ordinary sentiment sinks and drowns in this, and is thereby endangered and ruined. As for the mixed desire: some people are attached to all five of these matters together. As for desire for the human mark itself: some people are attached to none of these five matters, but are attached only to the human mark as such — whether male or female — such that, though they may perceive the above five matters in someone, if that person is not the one they love, they still remain unattached; but should they encounter a person who suits their own fancy, they are able to abandon everything the world holds dear, and cast away body and life in an instant.

Desires of this kind, life after life, deceive and bewilder sentient beings, causing them to sink into birth-and-death, drown in the three evil destinies, and never obtain liberation. Should one be able to skillfully cultivate the nine contemplations as their antidote, thereby dissolving them away, the bandit of the six desires is scattered and broken, and one swiftly realizes nirvāṇa.

zh: 所以者何？初死想，破威儀、語言二欲；次脹想、壞想、噉想，破形貌欲；次血塗漫想、青瘀想、膿爛想，多破色欲；次骨想、燒想，多除細滑欲；九想，除雜欲及所著人相欲；噉想、散想、骨想，偏除人相欲。殘噉離散白骨中，不見有人可著故，以是九想觀能破欲結，瞋、癡亦薄。三毒薄故，九十八使山皆動，漸漸增進其道，以金剛三昧摧破結使山，得三乘道。九想雖是不淨觀，因是能成大事，譬如大海中死尸，溺人依之，即得度也。三、明攝法者，是九想法緣欲界身色、想陰攝，亦身念處少分，或欲界攝，或初禪、二禪攝。未離欲散心人得欲界繫，離欲人得色界繫，胮脹等八想欲界初禪、二禪中攝，淨骨想欲界初禪、二禪、四禪中攝。三禪中樂多，故無是想。
en: Why is this? The initial perception of death breaks the two desires of demeanor and speech; next, the perceptions of swelling, decay, and devouring break the desire for form and appearance; next, the perceptions of being smeared with blood, livid discoloration, and festering, for the most part, break the desire for color; next, the perceptions of bones and burning, for the most part, remove the desire for smooth touch; the nine contemplations as a whole remove the mixed desire and the attachment to the human mark itself; and the perceptions of devouring, scattering, and bones especially remove the desire for the human mark, since, amid the remains — devoured, scattered, and reduced to white bone — no human mark whatsoever is left to be found for attachment to fix upon.

Through these nine contemplations, one is thereby able to break through the fetter of desire, and anger and delusion, too, grow thin. As the three poisons grow thin, the very mountain of the ninety-eight proclivities is shaken, and one gradually advances further along the path, until, with the vajra samādhi, one shatters the mountain of the fetters outright and obtains the path of the three vehicles. Though the nine contemplations are themselves a contemplation of impurity, through them one is able to accomplish this great matter — like a corpse floating in the great ocean, upon which a drowning person may yet depend, and thereby be delivered across.

Third, clarifying their classification: this dharma of the nine contemplations takes the desire realm's own bodily form as its object, and is classified under the aggregate of perception, also forming a small portion of the mindfulness of the body. It is classified, variously, under the desire realm, or under the first and second dhyānas. A person of scattered mind not yet free of desire obtains it as belonging to the desire realm; a person already free of desire obtains it as belonging to the form realm. The eight perceptions — swelling and the rest — are classified under the desire realm and the first and second dhyānas; the pure perception of bones is classified under the desire realm and the first, second, and fourth dhyānas. Within the third dhyāna, happiness is abundant, hence this perception has no place there.

zh: 四、明九想趣道者，修九想有二種：若按事而修，此則但能伏欲界結，後別修十想以斷見思，成無學道。二者、若善修九想，即具十想，從事入理，此則不煩別約餘門修十想。所以者何？如行者觀人死時，動轉言語，須臾間忽然已滅，身體胮脹、爛壞、分散，各各變異，是則無常。若著此身，無常壞時，是即為苦。若無常苦不得自在者，是則無我。不淨、無常、苦、無我故，則世間不可樂著，觀身如是。食雖在口，腦涎流下，與唾和合成味，而咽與吐無異，下人腹中即為糞穢，即是食不淨想。以此九想觀觀身無常變易，念念皆滅，即是死想。
en: Fourth, clarifying how the nine contemplations lead toward the path: cultivating the nine contemplations is of two kinds. Should one cultivate them by their own concrete matter alone, this is able only to subdue the fetters of the desire realm — one must afterward separately cultivate the ten perceptions in order to sever the afflictions of view and thought, and accomplish the path of no-more-learning. Second, should one skillfully cultivate the nine contemplations, one is already complete with the ten perceptions as well, passing from concrete matter into principle itself — in which case there is no need, separately, through some other gate, to cultivate the ten perceptions as well.

Why is this? As the practitioner contemplates a person at the moment of death — moving and speaking one moment, and then, in an instant, suddenly gone, the body swelling, decaying, and scattering apart, each stage transforming into the next — this is precisely impermanence. Clinging to this body as its impermanence brings it to ruin is precisely suffering. Should this impermanence and suffering leave one without any freedom of one's own, this is precisely no-self. Through impurity, impermanence, suffering, and no-self, the world is thereby seen as nothing to delight in or cling to — the body contemplated in just this way.

Though food is taken into the mouth, the brain's own fluid flows down and mingles with saliva to form its taste, and swallowing differs not at all from vomiting — once it descends into a person's belly, it becomes excrement itself: this is precisely the perception of the impurity of food. Through these nine contemplations, contemplating the body's impermanent transformation, ceasing moment after moment: this is precisely the perception of death.

zh: 以是九想厭世間樂，知煩惱斷，即安隱寂滅，即是斷想。以是九想遮諸煩惱，即離想。以九想厭世間故，知五陰滅，更不須生，是處安隱，即是盡想。若能如是善修九想，即具十想，斷見、思惑，當知是人必定趣三乘道。復次，《摩訶衍》中說，若善修九想，開身念處門，身念處開三念處門，四念處開三十七品門，三十七品開涅槃門，入涅槃故，則滅一切憂苦。菩薩憐愍眾生故，雖於九想能入涅槃，而亦不取實際作證。
en: Through these nine contemplations, growing weary of worldly pleasure and knowing the affliction's own cessation, one attains peace and quiescence: this is precisely the perception of cessation. Through these nine contemplations, blocking every affliction: this is precisely the perception of detachment. Through these nine contemplations growing weary of the world, knowing that the five aggregates cease and need never arise again, this place itself being at peace: this is precisely the perception of exhaustion.

Should one be able to skillfully cultivate the nine contemplations in this way, one is already complete with the ten perceptions as well, severing the afflictions of view and of thought — one should know that this person is certain to advance toward the path of the three vehicles.

Furthermore, the Mahāyāna treatise says: should one skillfully cultivate the nine contemplations, this opens the gate of the mindfulness of the body; the mindfulness of the body opens the gate of the three remaining foundations of mindfulness; the four foundations of mindfulness open the gate of the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; the thirty-seven factors open the gate of nirvāṇa; and, entering nirvāṇa thereby, every sorrow and suffering is extinguished. The bodhisattva, out of compassion for sentient beings, although able, even through the nine contemplations, to enter nirvāṇa, nonetheless does not grasp at the ultimate so as to make it one's own final proof.

zh: 所以者何？若色中無味相，眾生即不應著於色；若色中無離相，今亦不應從色得解脫。以色中有味故，眾生則著於色；色中有離相故，眾生從色得解脫。而味不即離，離不即味，離味處無脫處，離脫處無味處，當知色即非縛非脫。爾時不隨生死，不證涅槃，但以大悲憐憫一切眾生，於此不淨觀中成就一切佛法。《大品經》云：「九想即是菩薩摩訶衍。」
en: Why is this? Should form possess no mark of savor at all, sentient beings ought not to become attached to form in the first place; should form possess no mark of detachment at all, one likewise ought not to obtain liberation from form either. It is precisely because form possesses the mark of savor that sentient beings become attached to form, and precisely because form possesses the mark of detachment that sentient beings obtain liberation from form. Yet savor is not itself detachment, nor is detachment itself savor — apart from the place of savor there is no place of liberation, and apart from the place of liberation there is no place of savor; one should know, then, that form itself is neither bondage nor liberation. At that time, one neither follows along with birth-and-death, nor grasps at the proof of nirvāṇa, but, solely through great compassion for every sentient being, accomplishes the whole of the Buddhadharma within this very contemplation of impurity. The Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra says: "The nine contemplations are themselves precisely the bodhisattva's own Mahāyāna."

The six desires are worth noting as a taxonomy in their own right — color, form, demeanor, speech, touch, and "the human mark itself" (attachment to a specific person regardless of their qualities: even when the other five qualities are present, there is no attachment unless it is the person one loves). The precise mapping of which contemplation counteracts which desire is a good example of this treatise's habitual move: turning what looks like a single undifferentiated practice into a diagnostic instrument, matched item-for-item to specific afflictions. The closing citation from the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra performs the same reframing move fascicles 7 and 8 already used for the six wondrous gates and the thorough-and-bright contemplation: even the starkest, most viscerally "Hinayana"-coded practice in the entire treatise is, in the end, folded into the Mahāyāna, on the strength of the argument that form is "neither bondage nor liberation" — attachment and liberation both depend on the same object, since form has both a mark of savor and a mark of detachment, yet savor is not detachment and detachment is not savor.

quiz.q: What are the six desires counteracted by the nine contemplations?
options: wealth, sex, fame, food, sleep, dharma
color, form, demeanor, voice, smooth touch, the human mark
quiz.why: The six are desire for color, form and appearance, demeanor, speech and voice, smooth touch, and the human mark itself.

quiz.q: What characterizes the desire for the human mark?
options: attached not to the five but to the person; unmoved by others, yet for the right person one would throw away everything, even life
quiz.why: Such people are attached not to the five features but to the person; without the beloved they remain unmoved, but for the right person they would abandon everything, even life. Attachment to all five is the mixed desire.

quiz.q: What does one with the desire for smooth touch love?
options: a soft, glossy body like down, warm in cold and cool in heat
quiz.why: They love a soft body with glossy skin like the softest down, warm in cold weather and cool in heat. The other options are speech, appearance, and demeanor.

quiz.q: Which two desires does the initial perception of death break?
quiz.why: The initial perception of death breaks the desires for demeanor and speech, since the dead have neither.

quiz.q: Which perceptions mostly break the desire for color?
quiz.why: The blood-smeared, livid, and festering perceptions mostly break the desire for color; swelling, decay, and devouring break form; bones and burning remove touch.

quiz.q: Why do the devouring, scattering, and bone perceptions especially remove the desire for the human mark?
options: they belong to the form realm
among devoured, scattered remains and white bones, no person is left to be attached to
quiz.why: Among the devoured, scattered remains and white bones, no human being is left to fix attachment upon.

quiz.q: Though an impurity contemplation, the nine accomplish a great matter. What simile is used?
options: a corpse in the ocean on which a drowning person can float across
quiz.why: Though a contemplation of impurity, it accomplishes the great matter, like a corpse in the ocean that a drowning person clings to and is carried across.

quiz.q: After the nine break the fetter of desire, with what is the mountain of fetters finally shattered?
quiz.why: As the three poisons thin, the mountain of the ninety-eight proclivities shakes, and with the vajra samādhi one shatters it and attains the path of the three vehicles.

quiz.q: In which stages is the pure bone perception found, and why not in the third dhyāna?
options: desire realm, first, second, and fourth dhyānas; the third has too much happiness
quiz.why: The other eight are in the desire realm and first two dhyānas; the pure bone perception also in the fourth; the third dhyāna, abounding in happiness, lacks it.

quiz.q: What two ways of cultivating the nine lead to the path?
options: by concrete matter it only subdues desire-realm fetters, needing the ten separately; cultivated well it includes the ten, passing from matter to principle
quiz.why: Cultivated by concrete matter alone it only subdues desire-realm fetters, and the ten must be cultivated separately; cultivated well it already contains the ten, passing from matter into principle.

quiz.q: How does skillful cultivation of the nine include the perception of the impurity of food?
options: in the mouth, brain fluid mixes with saliva to form taste; swallowing is like vomiting, and it becomes excrement
quiz.why: Though food is in the mouth, brain fluid mixes with saliva to make its taste; swallowing differs not from vomiting, and in the belly it becomes excrement.

quiz.q: How does cultivating the nine include the perceptions of cessation, detachment, and exhaustion?
options: knowing afflictions severed is cessation; blocking afflictions is detachment; knowing the aggregates cease not to arise again is exhaustion
quiz.why: Weary of worldly pleasure, knowing afflictions severed, is cessation; blocking afflictions is detachment; knowing the aggregates cease and need not arise again is exhaustion.

quiz.q: Though able to enter nirvāṇa through the nine, why does the bodhisattva not grasp it?
quiz.why: Out of compassion for beings, the bodhisattva, though able to enter nirvāṇa through the nine, does not grasp the ultimate as final realization.

quiz.q: What do the marks of savor and detachment in form each do?
options: savor makes beings attached; detachment lets them be liberated from form
quiz.why: Because form has savor, beings cling to it; because it has the mark of detachment, beings are liberated from it.

quiz.q: From savor and detachment, what is concluded about form?
options: form is neither bondage nor liberation
quiz.why: Savor is not detachment and detachment not savor, yet neither exists apart from the other, so form is neither bondage nor liberation.

quiz.q: What does the Larger Sūtra say the nine contemplations are?
quiz.why: Within this contemplation of impurity one accomplishes all the Buddhadharma; the Larger Sūtra says the nine contemplations are the bodhisattva's Mahāyāna.
